S1 — BLOCKING: close_combat_instance falsely promises release/detachment of durable effect relationships.
Invariant/authority: every declared lifecycle operation and boundary must truthfully describe the existing engine (owning DESIGN D1/D2 and acceptance criteria; ADR 0020 section 3). The selected bonded-summon responsibility is also source-backed by spell:find-steed and spell:find-familiar in records.json and the vendored SRD p.143.
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:666.
Concrete scenario: the committed bondedSummonRecast.test.ts:133 creates a steed bond, vanishes the steed at 0 HP, closes combat, then recasts Find Steed successfully on the SAME actor; the effect and actor ownership link remain active and a new encounter admits that actor. The inventory instead says owned summon links are released and combatant source pointers detached. activeEffects.ts:7139 first rebinds durable combatant references onto campaign actors; :6736 migrates active actor/condition links, targets and source pointers without releasing them. Only REMAINING INSTANCE-ONLY references are released/removed/detached at :7152 onward.
Sibling analysis: distinguished durable versus instance-only combatants, active/pocketed/absent bonded actors, surviving versus ended/suppressed effects, actor and condition links, targets and source pointers, round/participant-clock expiry and concentration cleanup. Bonded-summon transitions use the same rebinding helper. Timer/concentration settlement precedes rebinding, so the survivor description must preserve those exceptions as well. The adjacent recast/transition/start/join contracts do not cure the contradictory close contract.
Required closure: describe the actual ordered lifecycle, explicitly retaining/rebinding durable topology before cleaning instance-only references; reconcile surviving character-owned effects with timer settlement and concentration cleanup. Preserve runtime behavior and source-backed continuing bond identity. Reconcile engine-capability-ownership's accepted reasoning after truthful inventory repair.
Permanent evidence: generalized topology/ownership and lifecycle invariants already exist in encounterCombatants.test.ts, activeEffects.test.ts, bondedSummonTransitions.test.ts and bondedSummonRecast.test.ts; the cited steed example directly preserves the source-backed recast claim. Point to appropriate existing evidence; no new per-tool behavioral suite or runtime repair is required.
Repair material: YES — changes the authoritative ownership/lifecycle guarantee. Owner: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12.

S2 — BLOCKING: campaign-rules-binding-store assigns persistence and incomplete inputs to a pure checker.
Invariant/authority: operation, required inputs and named engine surface must describe the same actual capability (owning DESIGN D1/D2 and acceptance criteria; ADR 0020 section 3), the same boundary invariant implicated by prior S5.
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:1877, :1882 and :1883.
Concrete scenario: checkBindingAgainstModuleRequirements(binding, compatibleRequirements) returns undefined and persists NOTHING. rules/binding.ts:69 is a pure check with no database parameter. The separately implemented writeCampaignRulesBinding(db, binding), :46, writes the single row; campaign/campaign.ts:70 checks first and :83 separately writes inside the creation transaction. The inventory names only the checker as operationId/entryPoint, promises persistence, and declares only binding and requirements, omitting the database needed for that operation.
Sibling analysis: checked default/stored binding resolution, compatibility failures by system/version/add-on, successful checking and actual campaign creation persistence. Grouped engine entries (sheet store, campaign-rule store, checkpoint store and item-reset executor) may legitimately cover related methods, but must identify the independent performed operations and their applicable inputs. This is not a demand for one entry per helper: the pure check cannot perform the advertised write, and the proposed inputs cannot supply it.
Required closure: give persistence/checking truthful callable identities and path-specific inputs, including the database for writes. Either distinguish the contracts or explicitly describe a correctly identified grouped boundary and its separate callable operations. Do not credit the pure checker with persistence or new atomicity. Preserve current runtime behavior and non-duplicated capability membership.
Permanent evidence: generalized compatibility and persisted campaign-binding invariants are already protected by campaignRulesBinding.test.ts and campaign.test.ts. Retain/reference those actual boundaries; no dedicated new helper test or AST checker is required.
Repair material: YES — changes authoritative operation/input/surface meaning. Owner: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12.

S3 — BLOCKING: positively selected cross-campaign character custody and revision operations are omitted.
Invariant/authority: the inventory must enumerate every in-force selected deterministic operation, including identity/ownership and persistence (owning acceptance criteria and DESIGN D1; ADR 0020 section 3). ADR 0012, docs/adr/0012-character-continuity-and-custody.md:96 onward, positively assigns linear revisions and a single active campaign writer, owner-checked sync/release, guarded resume, catch-up and explicit timeline forks to core.
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:1441 (ENGINE_PATHS), particularly :1583, :1611 and :1643; characterCustody.ts and characterRegistry.ts are absent from all inventoried runtimeOwner/engine surfaces.
Concrete scenario: Mira checked out to campaign A cannot also be checked out to campaign B or a second party slot: characterCustody.ts:165/:175 refuse before attaching. characterCustody.test.ts:480 asserts B remains unattached and A retains custody. CLI playCharacter.ts:282 consumes checkout, :673 consumes guarded resume, playClose.ts:42 releases custody, and playFork.ts consumes explicit new-identity forks. None of those ownership decisions is inventoried. character-sheet-attach-v1 describes only the lower-level sheet attach; it neither checks the registry lock nor enumerates this capability. Likewise the per-campaign sheet store does not describe append-only global revisions or owner-checked sync-back/release.
Sibling analysis: bounded missing family is registry-backed character continuity: initial registration/revision, checkout (other campaign versus same campaign/same or different slot), unchanged versus changed sync-back, stale/non-holder release, held-elsewhere/stale-head resume with per-turn state preserved, catch-up and separate-identity fork. Checked their implementations, registry persistence, ADR requirements, CLI producers and characterCustody/characterRegistry evidence. The existing attachment/import/persistence entries cover projections, not this ownership/revision boundary. These are already implemented and live, not unselected backlog. D3's refusal to claim universal engine-code closure does not exempt identified selected operations; no symbol census or per-helper contract is demanded.
Required closure: inventory this finite selected continuity family with truthful, non-duplicated W13 contracts (appropriately grouped where justified), actual inputs, refusals/ownership, revision semantics, owners and existing evidence. Reconcile the accepted engine-capability-ownership reasoning. Do not implement new custody behavior or add model-facing rule bindings.
Permanent evidence: generalized single-writer, revision continuity, stale-owner no-op, resume and fork invariants already exist in characterCustody.test.ts and characterRegistry.test.ts; reuse those pointers rather than adding near-identical reproducers.
Repair material: YES — authoritative in-force membership expands to cover omitted selected responsibilities. Owner: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12.
